draft.title: Area of a parallelogram
card: A parallelogram has two pairs of parallel sides. Its base is one of its sides. Its perpendicular height is the straight distance from the base up to the opposite side, at a right angle to the base.
The slanted side is not the height. The height is always measured at a right angle to the base.
Cut a triangle off one end and slide it to the other end. The shape becomes a rectangle with the same base and the same height.
So the area of a parallelogram is base \(\times\) perpendicular height. Example: base 9 cm and height 4 cm give \(9 \times 4 = 36\) cm squared.
draft.remember: Area of a parallelogram is base times perpendicular height, never the slanted side.

a.q: Why does a parallelogram have the same area as a rectangle with its base and perpendicular height?
opts: A cut-off triangle can be moved to make a rectangle
Its slanted sides are the same length as the height
Its area is half of the rectangle with the same sides
Its four angles can all be turned into right angles
a.why: Moving the triangle from one end to the other makes a rectangle without changing the area. The rectangle has the same base and the same perpendicular height. The slanted side is longer than the height, so it is not the same as the height.
a.clue: Think about what happens when you cut and slide a triangle.

b.q: Priya's garden bed is a parallelogram. Its base is 8 m, its slanted side is 5 m and its perpendicular height is 4 m. What is its area?
opts: 32 square metres
40 square metres
16 square metres
20 square metres
b.why: Area is base times perpendicular height, so \(8 \times 4 = 32\). The tempting answer is 40, which uses the slanted side of 5 m instead of the perpendicular height.
b.clue: Which of the given lengths is at a right angle to the base?
